Jamal Whitaker

gap-002 · supplement · fictional age 16

Written life first, then interpreted by a separate response author without the engine or results. These are synthetic checks. There is no correct career answer key.

Life from age 4 to 16

I am good with my granddad because I know him. I do not know if that means I am good with old people generally. Biology makes sense when somebody draws it, and then I can say it back. A blank report page is different. Mostly I want a normal week where we know who is doing what and I get to play music without checking my phone every ten minutes.

  • family: Lives with his mother, grandfather, and older sister; father lives in another Texas city and calls regularly.
  • finances: Rent and basics are usually covered; extra work hours sometimes disrupt family plans.
  • geography: San Antonio, Texas; previously lived in Waco.
  • cultureLanguages: English-speaking Black family with church connections; Jamal attends for relatives and music more than certainty about belief.
  • school: Public high school; plays trombone and receives ordinary classroom support for organization.
  • accessOpportunities: Library internet, school music lending program, family health appointments, and limited transport after school.
  • Age 4–5

    Jamal remembers building couch forts with his sister and asking his grandfather to be the monster. His grandfather usually fell asleep halfway through. Jamal liked replaying the same chase with a different ending, and he was furious when adults suggested that he was getting too big for the game.

  • Age 6–7

    At six he learned to make toast and carry a cup without spilling. His mother praised his careful walking, but school worksheets vanished in his backpack. He wanted to sit beside older cousins at family gatherings, listening to stories even when he did not understand why everyone laughed.

  • Age 8–9

    His grandfather developed a recurring leg wound when Jamal was eight. Adults handled treatment. Jamal asked why skin sometimes closed and sometimes did not, then forgot the question when a neighbor brought a scooter. Later he drew a lopsided diagram after finding a library book about circulation.

  • Age 10–11

    At ten he started trombone because the school could lend one. He disliked the first months of cracked notes but loved being inside a loud group. During his grandfather’s appointments he kept him company and wrote down questions the adults wanted to remember, without deciding which treatment was appropriate.

  • Age 12–13

    A move to San Antonio at twelve separated him from his closest friend. They played online most evenings until their schedules drifted. He became more interested in how infection spreads after a classroom experiment, but his lab reports were incomplete because he enjoyed discussion and neglected the written conclusion.

  • Age 14–15

    At fourteen he regularly prepared his grandfather’s lunch and checked whether a requested item was within reach. He resented missing band socials, then felt guilty about resenting it. His sister arranged a schedule so he was not the automatic helper. That made him more willing to sit and talk afterward.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen he can explain basic circulation from school and notices when his grandfather seems unusually tired, which he reports to an adult. He enjoys conversation with older people but finds repeated instructions irritating. He plans to finish high school with band and hopes to stay within visiting distance of family afterward.

Life now

  • enjoys: Band rehearsals · Body-system explanations · Long conversations with his grandfather
  • avoids: Writing up work after the exciting part · Being assigned help without discussion
  • activities: School band · Preparing simple lunches · Online games with school friends
  • demonstratedSkills: Keeps a practiced music part in time · Makes a simple meal independently · Records questions accurately when prompted
  • unfamiliarActivities: Formal caregiving training · Research laboratory routines · Living away from relatives
  • motivations: Belonging to a reliable group · Being useful without being taken for granted
  • ambitions: Finish high school with band · Live near relatives as a young adult
  • struggles: Missing written assignments · Mixed feelings about family duties · Changing friendships
  • supports: Sister who shares responsibility · Band director · Regular calls with his father
  • practicalConstraints: Bus schedules limit activities · Household schedules depend on work shifts · Care tasks sometimes compete with practice

Still uncertain: How much of his enjoyment of care comes from this particular relationship? · Would structured writing support change his experience of science classes?

Six scores & initial pathways

R, I, A, S, E, C: 20 / 23 / 24 / 22 / 20 / 17, each out of 40. Interests, not ability or success odds.

Pathways: None featured.

Work-led options: Design & creativity · Health & helping · Teaching & learning

Field explored: health. Jamal is curious about circulation and enjoys keeping his grandfather company. He wants to explore observing daily care to test whether that enjoyment extends beyond a close relative; this does not erase resentment of imposed duties or establish willingness to enter nursing training.

Conditional plan preview

Conditional preview of the first displayed career, to test preparation and money. This is not a student choice or a correct-career answer key.

Career: Registered Nurses

Preparation: Texas RN license or valid compact privilege.

  • Graduate from an approved nursing program.
  • Pass NCLEX-RN and the Texas nursing law exam.
  • Complete the Board application and fingerprinting.

Training budget before aid: $111,516 · 3.0 study years in this reference

Still needs funding: $111,516 · loan payments $0/month · included in lifestyle: no

Annual pay before tax: $74,370 · TWC entry-wage proxy · entry

Chosen-life income range: $60,000–$75,000

Budget result: This pay covers your lifestyle. Your costs and savings fit, with money left over.

Financial assumptions: Living within visiting distance of relatives is explicit, but tenure, home size, transport, food, travel, clothing, and saving levels are unknown. A modest rented apartment near useful transit, everyday groceries, a weekly casual meal, a modest getaway, a simple hobby budget, basic clothing, and savings index 2 are reference choices. Entertainment index 2 leaves room for music with others, a continuation wish inferred from keeping band; it is not a stated demand for frequent paid concerts.
